## What REST cannot see (master list)

The honest WordPress-CLI delta — everything a REST-only tool like this skill is blind to.
The other docs reference the relevant subset; this is the complete ceiling.

- **Exact WordPress core version** — REST exposes only an approximate/inferred version
  (see `01-site.md`).
- **Server stack** — PHP, MySQL/MariaDB, web-server (Apache/Nginx) versions; OS; memory
  limits; the database size, table prefix, and any custom (non-WP) tables.
- **`wp-config.php` constants** — `WP_DEBUG`, `DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT`, `WP_MEMORY_LIMIT`,
  auth salts, the DB table prefix, and every other defined constant.
- **Cron events** — the scheduled-task table (`wp_cron`) is not REST-readable.
- **Theme internals** — the theme file tree, `functions.php`, the template hierarchy,
  block patterns, and enqueued styles/scripts (all on disk).
- **ACF field-group definitions** — the *schema* (groups, field keys, field types,
  conditional logic). Individual field *values* on a post may be visible via
  `?context=edit` when registered `show_in_rest`, but the group structure is not.
- **Page-builder data shape** — `_elementor_data` (and equivalents) is an opaque blob;
  REST sees the meta field exists but not a model this skill can safely edit.
- **Plugin settings in `wp_options`** — active/inactive state is visible to admins; the
  configuration each plugin stores is not.
- **Must-use plugins / dropins** — not reported by the plugins endpoint.
- **CPTs / taxonomies registered `show_in_rest: false`** — **invisible to REST
  entirely.** The site may have more content types than the scan can see (see
  `02-content-model.md`). This is the most important blind spot: absence from these docs
  is not proof of absence on the site.
